summary: This bill amends title 31 of the U.S. Code to automatically continue funding for federal programs, projects, and activities at 94% of the prior year's rate (declining 1% every 90 days) if regular appropriations are not enacted by the start of a fiscal year, with the funding continuing until a new appropriations law is passed.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes automatic continuing resolutions that fund discretionary programs at 94% of the prior year's rate, with further 1% reductions every 90 days until an appropriations bill passes. This mechanism directly and automatically reduces government spending levels in the absence of new legislation, making spending reduction a core feature of the bill.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any changes to the tax code.
The bill addresses general appropriations procedures and does not target or alter funding mechanisms specific to healthcare programs or policy.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill makes no changes to immigration law, border policy, or related funding streams.
The legislation does not address reproductive health services, abortion access, or any related restrictions or protections.

While the automatic CR mechanism would apply to defense accounts, the bill is a general procedural change applying equally to all discretionary spending and does not specifically increase, decrease, or restructure military funding policy.
The bill contains no environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions and does not alter environmental funding or rules.

Subsection (a)(2)(C) explicitly maintains entitlement and mandatory programs (including Food and Nutrition Act programs) at full current-law levels, shielding them from the across-the-board reductions applied to discretionary accounts. This is a neutral preservation measure rather than an expansion or contraction of the safety net.
No education-specific policies, funding formulas, or school-choice provisions are included.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-related programs.
No provisions touch sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal-justice reform.
The legislation is silent on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.

By imposing automatic, declining spending caps until regular appropriations are enacted, the bill creates a structural incentive to limit outlays and thereby reduce deficits and slow debt accumulation.
The bill contains no civil-rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ-specific language.
No changes are made to foreign-assistance accounts or policy.
The bill does not address voting procedures, election administration, or voter-access rules.
No technology, data-privacy, or regulatory-oversight provisions are present.
The legislation does not alter labor law, collective-bargaining rights, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil-rights statutes and religious liberty.
